comments.author: @johntravis3242
comments.text: No. East is a direction, not a point. If you are measuring from the center of the country, it is Maine. The date lines have nothing to do with what is east and west other than direction. You asked a question about direction and got an answer referring to direction, then pompously claimed a technicality based on the location of imaginary man-made boundaries that doesn't hold up to simple fact. Your ignorance astounds.

replies.author: @Anakinspadawan1
replies.text: @johntravis3242  brother, Alaska extends into both the eastern and western hemispheres because the Aleutian Islands cross the 180th meridian. Maine doesnt extend into the eastern hemisphere, so Alaska can legitimately be considered both the easternmost and westernmost state by that geographic definition. also, who said anything about east and west being locations? nobody. youre arguing against something nobody claimed. and "if we only take a map of the country alone" is itself a technicality. youre choosing a localized reference point to determine the directions. your answer relies on a particular interpretation just as much as theirs does. both interpretations can be valid depending on the criteria. youre the one insisting that your interpretation is the only "scientifically correct" one, without actually understanding the geographic reasoning behind it. no one is wrong is here, but you are the only one who wants to be right.

replies.author: @johntravis3242
replies.text:
​@Anakinspadawan1 They aren't on a technicality. They are wrong in a literal directional sense. East and West are not locations like North and South. They are only directions. At no point while one is traveling west does it suddenly become traveling east. If take the *DIRECTIONS* as locations like some may just by looking at a traditional map of the world, then the video poster's idea would be accurate, *but* if you are taking a map of the country alone, starting from the innermost point, and choosing the points at the furthest east and west extremities *from that initial point*, you would have the *correct* answer that the video author claims is wrong. 

The point of the video was that the author was trying to sound smarter than his audience, and only managed to prove that he fails to understand basic science and geography when answering a localized question on a localized scale by stating that the "real" answer is a technicality based on a general scale of a man-made system rather than the much simpler, scientifically supported answer. 

If someone wants to get pedantic in their own ignorance, I am often willing to be petty right back. I felt so inclined here.

replies.author: @Anakinspadawan1
replies.text: they never said east was a point.. but youre also missing the point. east and west is determined by longitude, like after 180° E, the longitude becomes 179° W. because it wraps around. and Alaska holds both the Aleutian Islands which cross the 180° meridian. they arent wrong. so yes Alaska is the eastern and westernmost.
